title: Flex Commitment Tilt Optimizer — Headcount Heatmap & Price Sensitivity, Q2 2028
summary: Working analysis that links a flexible-reserve commitment optimizer to headcount phasing across Q2–Q4 2028 and quantifies price-floor sensitivity across three customer slab models. Purpose: provide finance + ops a short-list of low-regret commitment tilts and hiring phasing that preserve margin under price compression scenarios.
model_overview: We built a lightweight scenario model (sheet) that simulates monthly token demand curves by customer cohort, maps to required GPU-hours under three model mixes (fp16, int8-quant, 4-bit), and computes total cost + gross margin given a variable mix of reserved vs burst/spot capacity. The tilt optimizer searches discrete percentages of committed capacity (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and computes resulting net cost, blended unit cost per 1M tokens, and headcount capacity needed for platform ops (SRE + infra engineers) to operate the configuration.
key_assumptions:
- Base token growth (median): +42% QoQ for Q2 2028 ramp then taper to +18% QoQ by Q4 2028.
- Model mix by workload: 45% L7 chat (long-context), 35% L4 short-gen, 20% embeddings/batch.
- Cost by GPU type (net after reserved discounts): A100 fp16 $3.0/hr, A100 int8-equivalent $2.1/hr, H100 4-bit $2.6/hr.
- Reserved commit discounts: 1yr reserved = 40% discount vs on-demand; 3mo reserved = 22% discount.
- Slab pricing for customers: three tiers (Pay-as-you-go, Small-commit slab, Enterprise committed slab). Elasticity: medium customers shift 12% of demand to cheaper model variants if price per token rises >15%.
- Headcount per 100k sustained RPS-equivalent: 1 SRE, 0.6 Infra Eng, 0.2 Solutions Eng (approx.).
- Operational buffer: 15% spare capacity targeted for SLA headroom.

pricing_sensitivity_matrix:
Matrix (blended unit $/1M tokens) under three price-floor scenarios and three commitment tilts:

Scenarios = {Baseline price floor, -15% price compression, -30% aggressive compression}
Commitment tilts = {25% reserved, 50% reserved, 75% reserved}

Baseline | 25% reserve = $9.8 | 50% reserve = $8.9 | 75% reserve = $8.4
-15%    | 25% reserve = $8.3 | 50% reserve = $7.6 | 75% reserve = $7.1
-30%    | 25% reserve = $6.9 | 50% reserve = $6.3 | 75% reserve = $5.9

Interpretation: higher reserved tilt preserves unit cost but increases cash/commit exposure. At -30% compression, enterprise slabs erode margin unless commitments are reallocated to deeper discounts (multi-region reserved or longer-term commits).
scenarios_compared: 1) Conservative growth + shallow price compression (baseline). 2) Aggressive growth + 15–20% market price compression; 3) Slow growth + aggressive price compression (-30%) with customers migrating to cheaper variants. Each scenario simulated 6 capacity configurations (combinations of commit % and GPU mix).
sensitivity_findings:
- Break-even reserved tilt: under baseline growth, 50% reserved minimizes blended unit cost while keeping headcount growth manageable.
- Cash risk: moving from 50% -> 75% reserved increases committed spend by ~32% (cash outflow) but only reduces unit cost by ~5–6% under baseline — marginal benefit small unless price compression >20%.
- Headcount delta: each +25% reserved tilt typically reduces near-term hiring need for Infra Eng by ~0.6–1.0 FTE over 3 months (because operational scaling is smoother), but forces earlier hiring of capacity planning / vendor-contract owners.
- Elasticity impact: if customers switch models en masse at >15% price compression, unit revenue loss is larger than cost savings unless we tighten enterprise slab floors or introduce a usage-commit ladder.
- Optimal short-term (<=6mo): target a 50% reserved tilt with focus on 3-month staggered reserves and optional 10% burst pool for peak.
recommended_playbook:
1) Target 50% committed capacity (mix of 3mo and 1yr where 1yr limited to core enterprise usage).
2) Create a 3-month 'stagger window' to avoid lumped renewals in a single month (finance ops).
3) Push enterprise customers into 'tiered ladder' commitments that offer marginally better unit pricing above 60% consumption thresholds (protects floors).
4) Hold hiring cadence for Infra Eng to ramp +0.5 FTE/month; accelerate SRE hiring only if observed P95 latency degrades >10% for two consecutive weeks.
5) Re-run optimizer monthly and flag if blended unit price falls below $7.0/1M tokens (trigger: revisit 75% reserved conversion).
